support.text: You have a receipt for the full 30,000 INR deposit.
support.reason: The law text (BSA2023_s63_1) states that computer output may be deemed a document and admissible in proceedings if conditions are satisfied, but it does not mention anything about a 'receipt for the full 30,000 INR deposit.' The specific amount and receipt are not contained in the law text.

support.text: The owner must give you a certificate with your electronic record if you use it as evidence in court.
support.reason: The law text (BSA2023_s63_4) states that 'a certificate doing any of the following things shall be submitted along with the electronic record at each instance where it is being submitted for admission,' but it does not specify who must give the certificate (it does not say 'the owner must give you a certificate'). The sentence adds a condition about who must provide the certificate that is not in the law text.

support.text: Any electronic record, like a receipt photo or email, is considered a document in court if it meets the rules in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
support.reason: The law text (BSA2023_s63_1) states that 'any information contained in an electronic record...shall be deemed to be also a document, if the conditions mentioned in this section are satisfied in relation to the information and computer in question and shall be admissible in any proceedings.' The sentence states that 'Any electronic record, like a receipt photo or email, is considered a document in court if it meets the rules in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.' This is directly supported - the law text says electronic records are deemed documents if conditions are satisfied, and the sentence says they are considered documents if they meet the rules (i.e., conditions).

support.text: Free legal aid is available if your annual income is below 3,00,000 INR. You can call 15100 to find out if you qualify.
support.reason: The law text (LSA1987_s12) states that 'persons whose annual income is below the ceiling set by each State' are eligible for free legal services, and mentions 'NALSA's table shows Rs 3,00,000 for many States' as an example. However, the law text does not state that the ceiling is specifically 3,00,000 INR - it says it is 'set by each State' and gives examples. The sentence states 'if your annual income is below 3,00,000 INR' as a definite threshold, and adds 'You can call 15100 to find out if you qualify' which is not in the law text. The law text mentions 'Helpline 15100' but the sentence's conditional 'if you qualify' is an application not directly supported as a legal rule.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for return of security deposit

I paid you a security deposit of Rs 18,000 on [FILL: date paid] for the premises at [FILL: address]. I vacated the premises and handed over the keys on 15 September 2026. The deposit has not been returned.

I request you to return the deposit, less any deduction you can justify in writing with bills, within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If it is not returned, I will take legal action to recover it, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: Receipt for the deposit.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your rent agreement.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: none - this letter states facts only
